quote: Oh, looks like we've we've been speaking to you a couple days ago.
stewart_read: The rep acknowledges the record mismatch but doesn't resolve it — customer says the request was actually a month old, a discrepancy the rep never investigates (recycled lead misfiled as fresh?). The call moves on without correcting the record or probing why the timing is off.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep could have simply been reading from a CRM timestamp and had no reason to dig further since the customer answered the qualifying questions anyway.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to briefly clarify lead-age discrepancies — this may be a recycled lead with bill data possibly already on file, which changes how much re-collection is actually needed.

quote: I have I have received it, like, before, but, I don't know. It didn't convince me.
stewart_read: Customer discloses a prior solar design that failed to convince him. The rep asks when ("two or three years ago") but never asks WHAT wasn't convincing — price, savings numbers, company, panel type. This is exactly the competitive intel a closer would want.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep may be deliberately keeping this brief since it's setter scope and the closer will explore it in the design review.
coaching_implication: One follow-up question ("what part of it didn't work for you?") would give the closer a specific objection to address instead of walking in blind.

quote: In order to qualify for the current programs, all we ask of the homeowner is you just have a credit score of at least 670.
stewart_read: Rep states the credit threshold correctly at 670, matching the schema (unlike the 650 drift seen in other calls) and times the question efficiently while the customer is occupied pulling up his utility account.
coaching_implication: This is a positive example of stacking qualification into dead time — worth naming to the rep as a repeatable habit.

quote: Is there anybody else with title with you, or is it just My wife. Your wife.
stewart_read: Rep correctly identifies a co-owner (wife) on title but never returns to this fact when booking the appointment — the appointment is set with only Enrique's phone number, no mention of including his wife on the closer call.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep may judge this as low-risk since the wife wasn't raised as a decision-blocker (no 'I need to ask my wife' objection was voiced), so there was no protocol trigger to respond to.
coaching_implication: Even without an explicit objection, once a co-owner is identified the rep should ask if she'll be able to join the closer call — this is a structural gap that could leave the appointment vulnerable at proposal.

stewart_read: The usage data shows a steep winter climb (1,750 in January, 1,892 in February) against a summer peak of 1,280 in July — a wide, high-variance usage pattern that is strong solar-value material. The rep captures all twelve numbers but never reflects any of it back to the customer as a hook.
coaching_implication: Even a single line like 'wow, almost 1,900 kWh in February — that's a big winter jump, the specialist will want to build the system around that' would have anchored value in the moment instead of treating the numbers as pure data entry.

quote: That's exactly what we're looking for. So we are good to go in getting this design built out for you.
stewart_read: After collecting twelve months of granular usage data, the rep has maximum material to build curiosity ("once we see this pattern, we'll know exactly how to size this for you") but instead moves straight into scheduling with a generic close.
alternative_hypothesis: This may be deliberate scope discipline — the rep may be intentionally avoiding any hint of numbers/sizing talk to stay in setter lane and let the closer own that conversation entirely.
coaching_implication: There's a middle path between silence and scope creep — reflecting the pattern back builds anticipation without discussing pricing or specs. Coach the rep to try this softer version.
